questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

_____ burglars have been arrested but ____ jewellery is still missing.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blanks is (c). The definite article "the" is used before "burglars" to indicate that specific burglars have been arrested. The sentence refers to particular burglars known to both the speaker and the listener. Using "a" before 'burglars' is not right. It would mean that some random burglars have been arrested. Moreover, the indefinite articles 'a' and 'an' are used to modify singular nouns (not plural). The definite article "The" is also used before "jewellery" to specify a particular set of jewellery that is still missing. The use of 'a' before 'jewellery' would imply any piece of jewellery rather than a specific set of jewellery. The article 'an' can also not be used with 'jewellery' because this article is used before words that begin with a vowel sound. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

A noun is a word used as the name of a person, place, or thing. Now consider the following sentences:

1) Mahesh is a clever boy.

2) A herd of cattle was grazing on the pastureland.

3) Honesty is the best policy.

An article is a word that comes before a noun to indicate whether it's specific or general.

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.q_en:
In the given sentence, several segments have been underlined. One of these underlined segments is grammatically incorrect in the context of its usage in the sentence. Identify the incorrect segment from the following options.

He would never compromised his principles, even when faced with adversity, consistently upholding his integrity and staying true to his values.
questions.solution_en:
The verb "compromised" [past form verb] is incorrect because when "would" (modal verb) is used, the base form of the verb should follow. So, in this case, it should be "He would never compromise his principles" rather than "He would never compromised his principles."

The correct structure is "would never" + the base form of the verb. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The final correct sentence would be: He would never compromise his principles, even when faced with adversity, consistently upholding his integrity and staying true to his values.

Note: Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

There are too many spelling mistakes _____ this essay.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'in'. The preposition 'in' is used to indicate inclusion or containment within something. In the sentence, "There are too many spelling mistakes in this essay," 'in' accurately describes the location of the spelling mistakes, highlighting that they are contained within the essay. Other prepositions are not correct for the given context. The preposition 'on' is often used to indicate a surface or position in contact with a surface. The preposition 'at' is generally used to indicate a specific location or position. The preposition 'above' typically denotes a higher position in space or relative to something else. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

"A preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object."

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. These kinds of sharks are known as obligate ram ventilators because they draw water in through their mouths and force it out through their gills.

B. They use a method called buccal pumping, in which water is pulled in through the mouth and forced out through the gills by the cheek muscles.

C. It is true that many types of sharks must keep moving in order to receive life-giving oxygen from the water passing through their gills.

D. Other types of sharks are able to remain stationary because they possess special structures called spiracles, which force water out through their gills.
questions.solution_en:
'C' is the first sentence as it introduces the main subject 'types of sharks', it is followed by 'A' as it gives a name to the types of sharks mentioned in 'C'. How they breathe is mentioned in 'A' and what the whole process is called (i.e. buccal pumping), is mentioned in 'B'. 'D' is the final sentence as it talks about the other types of sharks that are stationary, so it is an independent sentence and can be used at the end of the paragraph. Therefore, the correct order of rearrangement is CABD.

Hence, option (a) is correct.
